action_items: Fix Home.jsx line 53-55: the base className contains 'bg-white' AND the conditional appends 'bg-[#1D4ED8]'. Tailwind's generated CSS order makes bg-white win (className order in string is irrelevant for CSS specificity). Change to conditionally choose the background, e.g. remove the literal 'bg-white' from base classes and use `${u.span ? 'bg-[#1D4ED8]' : 'bg-white'}` — OR use an important marker like '!bg-[#1D4ED8]'. Verify with computed style that backgroundColor is rgb(29,78,216) on both mobile and desktop after the fix.
critical_code_review_comments: Never combine two competing Tailwind utilities from the same category (e.g., `bg-white` + `bg-[#1D4ED8]`) on the same element and rely on className string order — Tailwind resolves conflicts via CSS source order, not JSX string order. Always branch the utility conditionally or use the `!` important prefix.

rca_of_the_issue: In /app/frontend/src/pages/Home.jsx (USPSection map, ~line 53-55), the featured card className string contains both `bg-white` in the base part and `${u.span ? 'bg-[#1D4ED8]' : ''}` appended at the end. Tailwind emits both classes; the winner is determined by the order of their rules in the compiled CSS file, not the order they appear in the className string. `bg-white` is defined later (or with equal specificity earlier) in Tailwind's generated stylesheet, so it overrides `bg-[#1D4ED8]`. Result: featured card is white-on-white on all breakpoints. Fix: make the background utility mutually exclusive per branch, e.g. `${u.span ? 'bg-[#1D4ED8]' : 'bg-white'}` and remove the standalone `bg-white` from the base classes.
